questions.note: Order is right in plan and V2o: hallux just ahead of toe 2 and touching it, toes 3-5 stepping back as the scan's, toe 5 rotated with its nail turned out, though it lies beside toe 4 rather than under it. Shaping fails: toes 2-4 are straight flat-topped blocks with no PIP knuckle, no curl and no pulp past the nails, with crisp slits, web notches, ringed undersides and crimped tips.

V8 is good: the lateral malleolus is lower, more prominent and further back, the medial higher; a clear Achilles cord with hollows either side over a bell-shaped heel, the column now centred over it. V3 shows the scan's hollow below the lateral malleolus. No anterior ankle crease shows at z 80-85 in V1f, V2 or V3, and the medial malleolus reads weak, as in the scan.

defects.what: Toes 2-4 are straight, flat-topped, parallel blocks of near-equal width with no PIP knuckle hump, no flexion at the middle and distal joints, and the nail running to the very tip with no pulp showing; the same finger look shows in V1f and in plan.
defects.fix: A booted man's lesser toes are slightly flexed: a rounded PIP hump 2-4 mm proud, the distal segment angled down onto a round pulp that bulges past and below the free edge, widths stepping down from toe 2 to toe 4, as in the scan beside it.

defects.what: From below, toes 2-4 are stacked cylinders cut by crisp transverse rings and fine striations, and toe 5 is crumpled into folds, instead of one plump plantar pad per toe behind a soft sulcus.
defects.fix: Each toe's underside is one smooth convex pulp pad, with at most a soft flexion crease at each joint, set off from the ball by a shallow rounded sulcus.

defects.what: In lateral view the lesser toe tips are low, flat and crimped, with sharp-edged steps at their ends; the scan's toes in the same view are round bulbs almost as tall as they are long.
defects.fix: Round each tip into a full pulp bulb about 10-12 mm tall, with the nail sitting on top of it rather than forming the end of the toe.

defects.what: Toe 5 meets the forefoot through a crisp vertical ring all round its base, like a tube plugged into a sleeve.
defects.fix: The fifth toe's skin runs into the lateral forefoot through a soft concave fillet, with at most a faint dorsal crease over the MTP joint.

defects.what: The hallux and toe 2 meet along a knife-cut V slit with hard edges from the web to the tips (also a crisp line in V4), not a soft skin contact.
defects.fix: Touching toes flatten slightly against each other: a closed contact line with a rounded shadow that opens into a smooth U at the web.

defects.what: Small hook-shaped notches sit at the roots of the 2-3, 3-4 and 4-5 webs, like pinched or folded geometry.
defects.fix: A web is a smooth U of skin between the bases of the toes, with no fold, hook or overhang.

defects.what: No anterior ankle crease shows at the dorsiflexion line (z 80-85): the shin turns into the dorsum with no fold in V1f, V2 or V3.
defects.fix: One transverse crease about 0.4 mm deep and 1.2 mm wide, bowed 3 mm toward the toes, with two or three fainter lines above it.

defects.what: Faint contour-like ripples on the back of the hallux near its medial edge read as a displacement artefact, not the soft wrinkles over the IP joint.
defects.fix: Two or three soft transverse wrinkles centred over the IP joint, fading toward the sides, and smooth skin elsewhere.

defects.what: A small sharp-edged mark on the hallux's plantar pad reads as a cut rather than a soft flexion crease.
defects.fix: The hallux pad is one smooth dome; its IP flexion crease is a soft, shallow transverse fold across the whole pad.

ranked: [D1] The lesser toes give the foot away: toes 2-4 are straight, flat-topped parallel blocks of one width, with no knuckle and no curl, the nails running to the tips. A booted man's lesser toes are slightly clawed and knuckled, each tip curling onto a round pulp.

[D3] In side view the lesser toes are low, flat, crimped strips where the scan's are round bulbs nearly as tall as they are long; the toe group reads thinner and more delicate than a 40-year-old soldier's.
[D2] From below the toes are stacked rings with fine striations and toe 5 is crumpled; real toes show one plump pad each behind a soft sulcus.

The sharpness is split: the scan-derived heel, arch, dorsum and ankle are soft and real, while the modelled toes carry hard-edged slits, rings and steps, so the toes look like a harder object grafted onto a real foot.
[D4] Toe 5 is plugged into the forefoot through a crisp ring at its base in V3; a real toe runs in through a soft fillet.
[D5] The hallux and toe 2 meet along a knife-cut V slit from web to tip; touching skin flattens into a closed, soft contact line.
[D6] Hook notches at the web roots of toes 2-5 in V5f read as pinched geometry; a web is a smooth U of skin.
[D7] No anterior ankle crease at the dorsiflexion line in any view; a standing man shows at least one faint transverse fold there.
[D8] Faint contour-like ripples on the back of the hallux read as a displacement artefact, not IP wrinkles.
[D9] A small sharp mark on the hallux's plantar pad reads as a cut.

Context: in V4 and V4o a mass from the leg above stands up to about 30 mm outside the medial border in front of the heel and hides the medial heel and arch outline from below; any of it below z 200 would be an ankle overhanging the arch.
